reason: Compared all source clauses of lem:wall-segment-stability and its proof with the compiled aggregate SM.wall_segment_stability and its concrete local definitions. The finite type of segment labels implements a genuinely finite family, including the harmless empty-family case. Each segment is represented by an initial point a i and oriented nonzero direction u i, with points a i+s*u i for 0<=s<=1. Continuity of these two functions is equivalent to continuity of the oriented endpoints. The only local-domain assumptions are continuity on an open neighborhood V of the centre t0 and nonzero central directions. This represents arbitrary continuous local segment families without requiring global continuity or assuming any persistence conclusion. All source families satisfy the hypotheses; asking nonzero directions only at the centre weakens the input and nonzeroness throughout the resulting U is proved. U is open, contains t0, and lies in V, so the conclusion is a genuine common neighborhood, not an empty or unrelated domain. SegmentPairPersists has the two exact central alternatives as conditional branches for every ordered pair: central disjointness implies nearby disjointness, and central transverse interior meeting implies TransverseIntersection nearby. It imposes no new restriction on singular pairs outside the source alternatives. segmentsMeet is actual closed affine segment intersection, equivalent to a common real-plane point by segmentsMeet_iff. Its stability is proved by a closed equality locus over the compact parameter square [0,1]^2 and closedness of the projection; no separation or stability property is assumed as an oracle. TransverseInterior means nonzero determinant and equality of the two actual affine points at strict interior parameters. TransverseIntersection includes nonzero determinant, both strict Cramer parameter bounds, the equality of their geometric points, and existence of exactly one common point of the closed segments. The Cramer formulas use det(b-a,v)/det(u,v) and det(b-a,u)/det(u,v), exactly the source signs and parameter assignments, and denominators are proved nonzero before continuity or cancellation is used. SegmentPairStableOn supplies ContinuousOn U for both parameter functions for every centrally transverse pair, not merely continuity at t0. Uniqueness and strict bounds hold on the same U as those continuities. CrossingOrderPersists compares the first parameters of two crossings on the same oriented first segment and assumes inequality only at the centre, exactly the source proviso. The aggregate quantifies every ordered triple, including exchange of the two crossing partners, so its less-than equivalences preserve strict order in both directions and exclude an equality appearing nearby when central parameters differ. Finite intersections of the nonzero, pair-persistence and all-triple order neighborhoods produce one U for all requirements. Specializing the arbitrary parameter space to the real line, openness at t0 gives a smaller common real interval; restricting the already-common-U conclusions supplies the final interval assertion of the source proof. No global regularity, smoothness, preselected persistent intersection, local transversality hypothesis or desired order law has been added. The formal proof is an alternative to the source distance estimate with the same geometry and conclusions. The audited semantic dependency inventory binds every predicate in the aggregate to its actual geometric definition. Only standard Lean axioms occur in the development audit. This independent review establishes full source fidelity separately from kernel checking; its supporting helpers are not additional original source claims.

stronger_than_source: Nonzero directions are assumed only at the centre (hnz, Lean line 121) while the source's 'nonzero oriented segments' (tex line 180) is a standing hypothesis on the family; Lean in addition concludes u i t ≠ 0 for all t in U (line 123).

Parameter space is an arbitrary topological space α (line 39), not the real interval the source proof has in mind ('one common interval', tex line 203), and continuity is required only on an open neighbourhood V of the centre (lines 119-120) rather than everywhere.

A single common open neighbourhood U ⊆ V carries every conclusion for the whole finite family (line 122); the source says 'nearby' clause by clause and only its proof remarks that one common interval works.

TransverseIntersection (lines 17-22) records explicitly that the Cramer parameters realise the common point and that the closed segments have exactly one common point (∃!), sharpening 'their unique intersection persists'.

The order clause is stated for all ordered triples (i,j,k) (line 125), so together with the swapped triple it yields strict order in both directions, excluding a nearby equality; the source's 'keeps its parameter order' is thereby realised in its strongest reading.
The empty family (ι empty) is allowed.
